mainTopic: A slave freed for an eye or a tooth, הכחשה and הזמה of witnesses, and a new משנה on when a thief pays ארבעה וחמשה, including admitting to a קנס
overview: The amud opens by finishing a question about a slave: if his master blinded his eye and knocked out his tooth, why not free him once for both? אביי answers from the פסוק that freedom is 'תחת עינו', for one injury only. רב אידי בר אבין then tries to prove from a משנה that הכחשה is the start of הזמה. The proof is pushed off, because the witnesses may have been made זוממין on the slaughter first. The גמרא shows this was already argued by רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר. It proves that רבי אלעזר says such witnesses are not killed. אביי then explains that רבי אלעזר's lashes apply when the 'murdered' man walks in alive. A new משנה lists cases where a thief pays כפל but not ארבעה וחמשה. The גמרא learns from it that a thief who admits can still be made to pay by later witnesses, which goes against רב הונא. רב חסדא challenges רב הונא from the story of רבן גמליאל and his slave טבי, and the debate continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why not free the slave for both eye and tooth?
steps.stepSummary: A challenger argues that when a master both blinds the eye and knocks out the tooth, the slave should go free for both injuries together, with no separate payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he blinded his eye, let the slave go free because of his eye. If he knocked out his tooth, let him go free because of his tooth. If he blinded his eye and knocked out his tooth, let him go free because of his eye and his tooth together!
steps.whatsHappening: Someone is challenging the idea that the master must pay for the second injury. He says that one release from slavery should simply cover both injuries.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each injury alone sets the slave free. So the challenger reasons that when both happen, the single release should count for both. If so, the master would owe nothing extra for the tooth.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him go out, meaning go free from slavery
He blinded
He knocked out his tooth

phrases.english: let him go free on account of his eye;
if he knocked out his tooth – let him go free on account of his tooth;

phrases.aramaic: סִימֵּא אֶת עֵינוֹ וְהִפִּיל אֶת שִׁינּוֹ –
phrases.english: if he blinded his eye and knocked out his tooth –
let him go free on account of his eye and his tooth!

steps.triggerLanguage: סִימֵּא אֶת עֵינוֹ וְהִפִּיל אֶת שִׁינּוֹ – נִיפּוֹק בְּעֵינוֹ וְשִׁינּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a challenge that began before this section, on the rule that the master pays for the second injury.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that when the master caused both injuries, the slave goes free for one and the master pays for the other.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each injury alone frees the slave, so one release should cover both and the master should owe no extra payment.

steps.title: אביי: the פסוק says 'for his eye,' not for both
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers from the wording of the פסוקים: the release is 'תחת עינו' or 'תחת שינו', for one injury, not for both together.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Against your claim, the פסוק says 'for his eye', and not for his eye and his tooth. It says 'for his tooth', and not for his tooth and his eye.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rejects the challenge by reading the exact words of the תורה. The release from slavery pays for one injury only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says the slave goes free 'תחת עינו', meaning in exchange for his eye alone. Freedom cannot pay for two injuries at once. So when there are two injuries, the slave goes free for one, and the master must pay damages for the other.

keyTerms.meaning: About you (your claim) the פסוק speaks, meaning the פסוק answers your argument
In exchange for his eye
In exchange for his tooth

steps.whatToRemember: Going free pays for only one injury. If a master blinds the eye and also knocks out the tooth, the slave goes free for one, and the master pays money for the other.

phrases.english: Abaye said: Against your claim, the verse states:
"For his eye" – and not for his eye and his tooth,
"For his tooth" – and not for his tooth and his eye.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1 with a reading of the פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One release from slavery could cover any number of injuries.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'תחת עינו' and 'תחת שינו' show that freedom pays for a single injury only, so the second injury needs a money payment.

steps.title: רב אידי בר אבין brings a proof from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב אידי בר אבין says the משנה about זוממין who testified on a theft and on the slaughter or sale supports רבא's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אידי בר אבין said: We too have learned this in a משנה. If someone stole, based on two witnesses, and slaughtered or sold, based on the same witnesses, and they were found to be זוממין, they pay him everything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the earlier discussion of רבא's view that הכחשה is the start of הזמה. רב אידי בר אבין says a משנה supports it, and here he quotes that משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the עדים זוממין pay 'everything'. That means the principal plus the extra four- or five-fold payment for slaughter or sale. Exactly how this proves רבא's point is explained in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned it in a משנה, meaning there is a source that supports this
Plotting witnesses, shown to be false because they were somewhere else at the time
Slaughtered or sold the stolen animal, which makes the thief pay four or five times
They pay everything, the full amount they tried to make him pay

phrases.english: Rav Idi bar Avin said:
We too have learned this:
If he stole, based on two witnesses,
and slaughtered or sold, based on them,
and they were found to be conspiring witnesses –
they pay him everything.
phrases.notes: That is the principal plus the extra four- or five-fold payment.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the slave question and goes back to the earlier discussion of רבא's view on הכחשה and הזמה.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that הכחשה is the start of הזמה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה (72b) about a thief convicted by two witnesses who were later found to be זוממין

steps.title: Reading the משנה as two testimonies and two הזמות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה is talking about witnesses who testified first on the theft and then on the slaughter, and were made זוממין first on one and then on the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not talking about a case where they testified about the theft, and then testified about the slaughter, and were made זוממין about the theft, and then were made זוממין about the slaughter?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes how to read the משנה so that it proves רבא's point. This sets up the proof, which step 5 completes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proposal is that the same pair of witnesses gave two separate testimonies and were proven false on each one in turn. If that is the case, the way the משנה treats the second testimony will show something about רבא's rule. The question 'מאי לאו' asks: isn't this the obvious way to read it?

keyTerms.meaning: What, is it not...? This proposes a reading of a source to use it as a proof
And they came back, meaning they did it again afterward
And they were made זוממין, proven to be plotting witnesses
Slaughter

phrases.english: What, is it not where they testified about the theft
and then testified about the slaughter,
and were made conspiring witnesses about the theft
and then were made conspiring witnesses about the slaughter?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the case in the משנה quoted in step 3, so it can be used as a proof.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that הכחשה is the start of הזמה
steps.raayaSupportSource: Reading the משנה as two separate testimonies, each proven false in turn

steps.title: The proof: they pay even for the slaughter
steps.stepSummary: Once the witnesses are made זוממין on the theft, their slaughter testimony is already contradicted. Yet the משנה says they pay everything, so הכחשה must be the start of הזמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once they were made זוממין about the theft, their testimony about the slaughter became contradicted. Yet the משנה says they pay everything. If contradiction were not the beginning of הזמה, why would they pay for the slaughter? So we must learn from this that contradiction is the beginning of הזמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof from the משנה, using the order of events described in step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there was no theft, killing the animal is not a crime, so the slaughter testimony falls apart the moment the theft testimony falls. The later הזמה on the slaughter only comes after that testimony is already contradicted. Since the משנה still makes them pay for the slaughter, a הכחשה followed by הזמה must still count as הזמה.

keyTerms.meaning: Contradicting witnesses about what happened, without proving they were somewhere else
Proving the witnesses were elsewhere at the time, which brings the punishment of עדים זוממין
The beginning of הזמה: a contradiction can be the first step, later finished by הזמה
Contradicted; their testimony no longer stands
Slaughtering the stolen animal, which brings the larger payment of four or five times

steps.confusionAlert: הכחשה and הזמה are not the same. In a הכחשה the witnesses' story is denied. In a הזמה the witnesses themselves are shown to have been elsewhere, and only הזמה brings the special punishment.

phrases.english: But once they were made זוממין on the theft
regarding the slaughter, they became contradicted,
phrases.notes: With no theft, slaughtering the animal is no crime, so the slaughter testimony falls apart.

phrases.english: and yet it teaches: they pay him everything.
And if it enters your mind
that contradiction is not the beginning of הזמה,
why do they pay for the slaughter?
Rather, must we not learn from it
that contradiction is the beginning of הזמה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof that step 4 set up by fixing the order of events.
steps.raayaObject: The view that הכחשה תחילת הזמה היא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: witnesses who testified on theft and slaughter and were found זוממין pay everything

steps.title: Pushing off the proof: they were made זוממין on the slaughter first
steps.stepSummary: The משנה can be talking about witnesses who were made זוממין on the slaughter before the theft, so no contradiction came first.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: what case are we dealing with here? A case where they were made זוממין on the slaughter first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by reading the משנה as a different order of events.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the הזמה on the slaughter came first, the slaughter testimony was never contradicted before it was found to be זוממין. That is a plain, ordinary הזמה. So the משנה tells us nothing about whether הכחשה is the start of הזמה.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? This is used to narrow a source to a specific case
First

phrases.english: They say: with what are we dealing here?
a case where they were made זוממין on the slaughter first,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 5's proof by reversing the order of the הזמות assumed in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the הזמה on the theft came first. The משנה can be read with the slaughter הזמה first, so no הכחשה came before it.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה does not prove that הכחשה תחילת הזמה היא, because it can be read as a case where the הזמה on the slaughter came first.

steps.title: An earlier dispute on the same question
steps.stepSummary: Whether witnesses who were first contradicted and later made זוממין are killed was already argued by רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is in a dispute. Witnesses who were contradicted and in the end made זוממין: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר argue. One says they are killed, and one says they are not killed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us that the same question was argued by earlier אמוראים. It names the two sides without saying yet who holds which.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The side that says 'they are killed' holds that the earlier הכחשה was the start of הזמה, so the later הזמה brings the full punishment. The side that says 'they are not killed' holds that once they were contradicted, a later הזמה does not count. The next step tries to figure out who holds which view.

keyTerms.meaning: A dispute
They are put to death, the punishment of זוממין in a capital case
One said; the גמרא gives the views without saying who said which

phrases.english: And it is in a dispute:
witnesses who were contradicted and in the end were made זוממין
Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Elazar:
one said: they are killed,
and one said: they are not killed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from the משנה fails, the גמרא shows the question is an older dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute between רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר whether witnesses who were contradicted and later made זוממין are killed.

steps.title: Suggesting that רבי אלעזר says they are not killed
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי אלעזר says contradicted witnesses in a capital case get lashes, it seems he is the one who says they are not killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It may be concluded that it is רבי אלעזר who says they are not killed. For רבי אלעזר said: witnesses who were contradicted in a capital case receive lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to figure out which אמורא holds which view, using another statement of רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר says contradicted witnesses in a capital case get lashes. The גמרא suggests this fits only with the view that a later הזמה would not bring death, so he would be the one who says אין נהרגין. The next step explains why lashes and the death penalty cannot go together.

keyTerms.meaning: It may be concluded; a suggestion that the גמרא may still look into
They receive lashes
In a capital case, where a life is at stake

phrases.english: It may be concluded that it is Rabbi Elazar
who says they are not killed
for Rabbi Elazar said:
witnesses who were contradicted in a capital case receive lashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּסְתַּיֵּים דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הוּא דְּאָמַר אֵין נֶהֱרָגִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to assign the two unnamed views from step 7 to their speakers.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אלעזר is the one who says אין נהרגין
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אלעזר's statement that witnesses contradicted in a capital case receive lashes

steps.title: Why lashes show that רבי אלעזר says they are not killed
steps.stepSummary: If רבי אלעזר held that contradicted witnesses can later be killed, he could not give them lashes, because a prohibition that can lead to court-imposed death never brings lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think רבי אלעזר is the one who says they are killed, why would they get lashes? Their prohibition would then be one that warns of death by the court, and you never get lashes for a prohibition like that!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the logic behind the proof from the last step. It shows why lashes and the death penalty cannot go together here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that a לאו which can lead to מיתת בית דין does not bring lashes. If רבי אלעזר held these witnesses could still be killed after a later הזמה, then their sin would be that kind of לאו. Since he says they get lashes, he cannot hold that they are killed.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you were to think: introduces an idea the גמרא is about to reject
They receive lashes

keyTerms.term: לָאו שֶׁנִּיתַּן לְאַזְהָרַת מִיתַת בֵּית דִּין
keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition given as a warning for death by the court
They are killed (executed)

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule, that a לאו leading to death never brings lashes, is the key that lets the גמרא decide which אמורא holds which opinion.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that it is Rabbi Elazar who says they are killed,
phrases.notes: "They" means witnesses in a death case who were first contradicted and only later made זוממין.

phrases.english: why are they lashed?
It would be a prohibition that was given
as a warning for death by the court,
and any prohibition that was given
as a warning for death by the court
one is not lashed for it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הוּא דְּאָמַר נֶהֱרָגִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the proof suggested in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אלעזר is the one who says contradicted witnesses later made זוממין are not killed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אלעזר's ruling that contradicted witnesses in a death case get lashes, together with the rule that a לאו leading to court-imposed death never brings lashes.

steps.title: Conclusion: רבי אלעזר says they are not killed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבי אלעזר is the one who holds that contradicted witnesses who are later made זוממין are not killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: So isn't it clear from this that רבי אלעזר is the one who says they are not killed? Yes, it is proven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the result of the proof and accepts it with the word תסתיים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since lashes and death cannot go together here, רבי אלעזר must say they are not killed. That means רבי יוחנן is the one who says they are killed. This settles who holds which side of the argument from step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it so: learn from this
It is proven: the גמרא accepts the conclusion

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר: witnesses first contradicted and later made זוממין are not killed (and they get lashes for the contradiction). So רבי יוחנן is the one who says they are killed.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it so? Learn from this

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הוּא דְּאָמַר אֵין נֶהֱרָגִין?
phrases.english: that it is Rabbi Elazar who says they are not killed?
It is proven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: States and accepts the result of the proof built in steps 8 and 9.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי אלעזר holds that witnesses who were contradicted first and later made זוממין are not killed.

steps.title: How can contradicted witnesses get lashes if it is two against two?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר's ruling that contradicted witnesses get lashes: when two witnesses say one thing and two say the opposite, why trust the second pair?
steps.simpleTranslation: They get lashes?! It is two witnesses against two. Why do you rely on these? Rely on those!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now questions רבי אלעזר's ruling itself. It asks how a court can punish the first witnesses just because two other witnesses disagree with them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In plain הכחשה, each pair simply says the opposite of the other pair. There is no reason to believe the second pair more than the first. So how can the court decide the first pair lied and give them lashes?

keyTerms.meaning: Two (witnesses) against two
What did you see: why choose this side over the other?
Rely on

steps.confusionAlert: This is not הזמה. In הזמה the second pair says the first pair was somewhere else, and the תורה tells us to believe the second pair. In plain הכחשה there is no such rule, so it is a real tie.

phrases.english: They are lashed?!
It is two against two,
what did you see that you rely on these?
phrases.notes: "These" are the second pair, the ones who contradicted the first witnesses.

phrases.english: Rely on these!
phrases.notes: Here "these" means the first pair: you could just as easily believe them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling רבי אלעזר's view, the גמרא challenges his ruling that contradicted witnesses get lashes.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's ruling that witnesses contradicted in a death case get lashes.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With two witnesses against two, there is no basis to call the first pair liars, so there is no basis to punish them.

steps.title: אביי: the "murdered" man walks in alive
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that רבי אלעזר is talking about a case where the man the witnesses said was killed comes to court on his own feet.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is a case where the "murdered" man came in on his own feet.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by narrowing the case. The contradiction is not just another pair of witnesses but the living man himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the man the witnesses said was murdered is standing in court alive, it is no longer two against two. Their testimony is clearly false, so the court can give them lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who was (supposedly) killed
On his own feet: alive and walking

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר's lashes for contradicted witnesses apply where the falsehood is certain, such as when the "murdered" man shows up alive.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
It is where the one who was "killed" came on his own feet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11 by limiting the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) to one where the falsehood is clearly proven
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Contradicted witnesses are just two against two, so no one can know who lied.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is one where the supposed victim shows up alive, so the first witnesses are clearly lying and get lashes.

steps.title: The theft is proven but the slaughter or sale is not
steps.stepSummary: If two witnesses proved the theft, but only one witness or the thief himself says he slaughtered or sold the animal, he pays כפל but not ארבעה וחמשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a person stole an animal, and this was proven by two witnesses, and then he slaughtered or sold it, but that was proven only by one witness or by his own admission, he pays double. He does not pay four or five times.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that the extra fine of four or five times needs the slaughter or sale itself to be properly proven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate fines here. The theft alone brings כפל, and that was proven by two witnesses. The slaughter or sale is what raises the payment to four or five times, so it also needs full proof. One witness or the thief's own word is not enough for that.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Double payment: the thief pays twice the value
Four times the value for a sheep, five times for an ox, when the thief slaughters or sells it
Slaughtered or sold
A single witness
Based on his own admission

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the thief gets off free. The theft was fully proven, so he still pays כפל. He only avoids the extra four or five times.

phrases.english: MISHNA: If he stole, based on two witnesses,

phrases.aramaic: וְטָבַח וּמָכַר עַל פִּי עֵד אֶחָד
phrases.english: and slaughtered or sold it, based on one witness
or based on his own admission –
he pays the double payment,
but he does not pay the fourfold or fivefold payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the sugya about עדים זוממין ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The four or five times fine needs the slaughter or sale to be proven by full testimony. Otherwise only כפל is paid.

steps.title: Four more cases that bring only double payment
steps.stepSummary: Slaughtering on שבת, slaughtering for עבודה זרה, stealing from his father who then died, and stealing then making it הקדש all bring כפל but not ארבעה וחמשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies if he stole and slaughtered on שבת, or stole and slaughtered for עבודה זרה, or stole from his father and then his father died and only after that he slaughtered or sold it, or stole and made it הקדש and only after that slaughtered or sold it. In all these cases he pays double and does not pay four or five times.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists four more cases with the same result: the thief pays כפל only. The משנה gives no reasons here; the גמרא will explain them later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In every case the theft is a normal theft, so כפל stays. Something about the slaughter or sale is unusual. Either the act itself is a serious sin, as on שבת or for עבודה זרה, or the animal's ownership changed before the slaughter, as with the father's death or הקדש. Because of that, the extra fine does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughtering on שבת is a sin that carries the death penalty
Idol worship
And he made it holy (הקדש), giving it to the Temple
And afterward: the change happened before the slaughter or sale

phrases.english: If he stole and slaughtered on Shabbat;
if he stole and slaughtered for idol worship;
if he stole from his father's property, and his father died,
and afterward he slaughtered or sold it;
if he stole and consecrated it,
and afterward slaughtered or sold it –
he pays the double payment,
but he does not pay the fourfold or fivefold payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more cases with the same result as step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In these four cases the thief pays only כפל and is exempt from ארבעה וחמשה.

steps.title: רבי שמעון splits the case of holy animals
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says: for קדשים the owner must replace, the thief pays ארבעה וחמשה; for קדשים the owner does not have to replace, he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: for holy animals that the owner is responsible to replace, the thief pays four or five times. For holy animals the owner is not responsible to replace, the thief is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון disagrees with part of the last case, the stolen animal that became הקדש. He splits it into two kinds of holy animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owner must replace the animal when it is lost, he is still the one who loses out. So it still counts as his animal for the fine, and the thief pays four or five times. If the owner does not have to replace it, it is not really his loss, and the thief is exempt from the extra fine.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy animals set aside as offerings
Responsible for them: the owner must replace the animal if it is lost
Exempt

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
sacrificial animals for which he bears responsibility,
he pays the fourfold or fivefold payment;
phrases.notes: Ignore the period after מְשַׁלֵּם. Read it together: 'he pays four or five times.'

phrases.english: for those he bears no responsibility for, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר קֳדָשִׁים שֶׁחַיָּיב בְּאַחְרָיוּתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion about the case of an animal that became הקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The thief pays ארבעה וחמשה for קדשים the owner must replace, and is exempt for קדשים the owner need not replace.

steps.title: Why teach the one-witness case? It is obvious!
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needed to say that one witness does not bring ארבעה וחמשה, since one witness never makes anyone pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: 'Based on one witness' — that is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It challenges the first line of the משנה, saying the one-witness case teaches nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows a single witness cannot obligate someone to pay. So of course he does not pay four or five times based on one witness. The גמרא is setting up its next move: explaining why the משנה still needed to say it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
It is obvious! Asking why something needed to be taught at all

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ עַל פִּי עֵד אֶחָד – פְּשִׁיטָא!
phrases.english: GEMARA: Based on one witness – that is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the first line of the משנה from step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's words 'על פי עד אחד'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A single witness never obligates payment, so teaching that he does not obligate ארבעה וחמשה seems pointless.

steps.title: One witness is mentioned to teach about the thief's own admission
steps.stepSummary: The משנה mentions one witness so that the thief's own admission will be read the same way: if witnesses come later, he must pay ארבעה וחמשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: The משנה is teaching us that 'based on his own word' is like 'based on one witness.' With one witness, if a second witness comes and joins him, the thief must pay. So too with his own word: if witnesses come later, he must pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 16. The משנה mentioned one witness on purpose, to teach us something about the thief who admits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One witness alone does nothing, but he is not cancelled. A second witness can still join him. By putting the thief's admission next to one witness, the משנה teaches that the admission also does not block witnesses who come later, and he will then pay ארבעה וחמשה.

keyTerms.meaning: Based on his own word (his own admission)
Similar to, the same as
Joins together (one witness with another to make two)
He becomes obligated to pay

phrases.english: They say: This is what it teaches us:

phrases.aramaic: עַל פִּי עַצְמוֹ – דּוּמְיָא דְּעַל פִּי עֵד אֶחָד;
phrases.english: 'based on his own word' is similar to 'based on one witness';
just as with 'based on one witness'
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording to make the phrase complete.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אָתֵי עֵד אֶחָד מִצְטָרֵף בַּהֲדֵיהּ, מִיחַיַּיב;
phrases.english: when another witness comes and joins with him, he becomes obligated;
so too with 'based on his own word':
when witnesses come, he becomes obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16 about why one witness was mentioned.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the wording is not extra. It teaches a hidden comparison between two cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Mentioning one witness seemed pointless, since one witness never makes anyone pay.
steps.terutzMaskana: One witness is mentioned to show that a thief's admission, like a lone witness, can be followed by witnesses who make him pay ארבעה וחמשה.

steps.title: This reading rejects רב הונא's ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that this reading of the משנה goes against רב הונא in the name of רב, who says that one who admits to a קנס is exempt even if witnesses come later.
steps.simpleTranslation: This comes to reject the view of רב הונא in the name of רב. For רב הונא said in the name of רב: One who admits to a קנס, and afterward witnesses come, is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out whose opinion the משנה, as just explained, disagrees with. That opinion is רב הונא's in the name of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 17 the משנה was read to say that witnesses who come after the admission still make the thief pay. רב הונא holds the opposite: once a person admits to a קנס, he is exempt for good, even if witnesses come later.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude, to reject (another opinion)
One who admits to something that carries a fine
A fine: a payment beyond the actual damage, like כפל or ארבעה וחמשה
Exempt, does not have to pay

steps.confusionAlert: Everyone agrees that a person does not pay a קנס based on his own admission. The argument here is about witnesses who come AFTER he already admitted.

phrases.english: This rejects what רב הונא said in the name of רב,
for רב הונא said in the name of רב:
One who admits to a fine,
and afterward witnesses came, is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out what step 17's reading of the משנה means: it disagrees with רב הונא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא in the name of רב: one who admits to a קנס is exempt even if witnesses come afterward. The משנה, as explained, disagrees.

steps.title: Looking at רב הונא's ruling by itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats רב הונא's ruling so it can discuss it on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now the matter itself: רב הונא said in the name of רב: One who admits to a קנס, and afterward witnesses come, is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to study רב הונא's ruling by itself. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling was only mentioned in passing before. Here it becomes the main topic, so it is repeated in full before the גמרא tests it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The thing itself': the גמרא returns to examine a statement it mentioned earlier

phrases.aramaic: גּוּפָא – אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: The matter itself: רב הונא said in the name of רב:
One who admits to a fine,
and afterward witnesses came, is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא – אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the ruling quoted in step 18 and makes it the new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Admitting to a קנס exempts a person, even if witnesses come later.

steps.title: רב חסדא challenges with the story of רבן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא begins a challenge to רב הונא from a story: רבן גמליאל blinded the eye of his slave טבי and was very happy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא challenged רב הונא: There was a story with רבן גמליאל, who blinded the eye of his slave טבי, and he was very, very happy.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא opens his challenge by bringing a story. This part only sets up the story. The point of the challenge comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A slave whose master blinds his eye goes free, and that freedom counts as a קנס on the master. רבן גמליאל was happy because now his slave could go free. The question will be whether his own admission, or witnesses later, can make that happen.

keyTerms.meaning: A story, an actual event
He blinded
His slave

phrases.english: רב חסדא raised a challenge against רב הונא:
There was a story with רבן גמליאל
who blinded the eye of טבי, his slave,
phrases.notes: A master who knocks out his slave's eye must set him free (שמות 21:26).

phrases.english: and he was very, very happy.
phrases.notes: He was happy because he wanted טבי to go free, and now he had a way to do it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the attack on the ruling quoted in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that admitting to a קנס exempts a person even if witnesses come later.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only. The story of the slave's freedom (a קנס) will be used to show that witnesses could still count after an admission.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: Your words mean nothing, since there are no witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל tells רבי יהושע that טבי went free because he blinded him. רבי יהושע answers that his words mean nothing, because there are no witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: He met רבי יהושע and said to him: 'Don't you know that my slave טבי went free?' He said: 'Why?' He said: 'Because I blinded his eye.' He said: 'Your words mean nothing, since he has no witnesses.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues and reaches its point. רבי יהושע says the admission alone does not free the slave, because there are no witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע gave the reason 'there are no witnesses.' That sounds like witnesses could still help, even after רבן גמליאל admitted. That would go against רב הונא, who says the admission exempts him for good.

keyTerms.meaning: Went out to freedom, became free
Your words mean nothing (have no legal effect)
I blinded

steps.whyThisMatters: This story is the source of the challenge to רב הונא. The exact wording 'there are no witnesses' is what the challenge is built on.

phrases.english: He met רבי יהושע and said to him:

phrases.aramaic: ״אִי אַתָּה יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁטָּבִי עַבְדִּי יָצָא לְחֵירוּת?״
phrases.english: "Don't you know that טבי, my slave, has gone free?"
He said to him: "Why?"
He said to him: "Because I blinded his eye."
He said to him: "Your words mean nothing,
since he has no witnesses."
phrases.notes: His own admission can't free the slave, because freedom here works like a קנס, and a קנס needs witnesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story begun in step 20 and gives the line the challenge depends on.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that admitting to a קנס exempts a person even if witnesses come later.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהושע's reason is 'there are no witnesses.' That suggests witnesses who come later would free the slave, even after the master admitted. This contradicts רב הונא.

steps.title: The inference from the טבי story contradicts רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא infers from רבי יהושע's words that if there were witnesses, רבן גמליאל would be obligated even after admitting. So a person who admits to a קנס is still liable when witnesses come later, which contradicts רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: So if he had witnesses, he would be obligated. We learn from this that someone who admits to a קנס, and later witnesses come, is obligated!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא finishes his challenge. He reads the story closely: 'no witnesses' means that with witnesses, רבן גמליאל would have to free טבי, even though he had already admitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע's reason was only that there were no witnesses. He did not say the admission itself exempts רבן גמליאל. So if witnesses showed up after the admission, the obligation would still apply. That is exactly the opposite of רב הונא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: We learn from it (an inference drawn from a source)
One who admits to an act that carries a fine
Witnesses

phrases.english: But if he has witnesses, he is obligated,
phrases.notes: This is read from רבי יהושע's words 'there are no witnesses.' Flip it, and with witnesses he would have to free טבי.

phrases.english: and we learn from it:
one who admits to a fine,
and afterward witnesses came, is obligated!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא יֵשׁ לוֹ עֵדִים – חַיָּיב, וְשָׁמְעִינַן מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב חסדא's challenge that began in steps 20-21 by drawing the inference from רבי יהושע's reply.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא in the name of רב: one who admits to a קנס is exempt even if witnesses come later.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהושע exempted רבן גמליאל only because there were no witnesses. That implies witnesses arriving after the admission would still obligate him.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל did not admit before a court
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that the case of רבן גמליאל is different, because his admission was not made in front of a בית דין. Only an admission in court exempts a person from a קנס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said to רב חסדא: רבן גמליאל is different, because he did not admit in front of a בית דין.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא defends his rule. He says the story does not prove anything, because רבן גמליאל's admission was not the kind that exempts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's rule applies only to an admission made in front of a בית דין. רבן גמליאל just told רבי יהושע privately, so his admission never counted. That is why only witnesses could matter in his case. This gives no proof about someone who admitted in court.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different (a way of separating one case from another)
In the presence of a court
He admitted

phrases.english: He said to him: Rabban Gamliel is different,
phrases.notes: רב הונא is the one speaking here, answering רב חסדא.

phrases.english: for he did not admit in front of a court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב חסדא's challenge in step 22 by showing the story's case is different.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case (שאני): the admission was made outside court.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבן גמליאל's admission was a real legal admission, so the story shows that witnesses coming afterward still obligate.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only an admission before a בית דין exempts from a קנס. רבן גמליאל's was outside court, so the story says nothing against רב הונא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets an important condition on רב הונא's rule: the exemption depends on admitting in front of a בית דין.

steps.title: But רבי יהושע was the head of the court
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הונא's answer. רבי יהושע was the אב בית דין, so telling him looks like admitting before a court.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי יהושע was the head of the court!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב הונא's answer. Since רבי יהושע headed the court, it seems רבן גמליאל did admit before a בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's answer depends on the admission having been outside court. But the person who heard it was the head of the court, which makes it sound like a court admission. If so, the difference רב הונא pointed to falls apart, and the challenge returns.

keyTerms.meaning: Head of the court, the second-highest leader of the סנהדרין
But surely (opens a challenge)

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אַב בֵּית דִּין הֲוָה!
phrases.english: But Rabbi Yehoshua was the head of the court!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אַב בֵּית דִּין הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that רבן גמליאל did not admit before a court.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Admitting to the אב בית דין looks like admitting before a court, so the case is not really different.
